In this excerpt (the opening of Franz Kafka's *The Metamorphosis*), Gregor Samsa is the only character present, and he is immediately established as a complex, round character. Rather than reacting to his transformation into a giant insect with one-dimensional horror, he displays a realistic and engaging mix of human traits: confusion, melancholy caused by the rainy weather, denial, and mundane frustration over not being able to roll onto his preferred sleeping side. Furthermore, brief details about his room—such as his cloth samples and the framed magazine cutout—efficiently provide backstory about his life as a traveling salesman and his personal habits, giving him depth right from the beginning.
